newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel budget talks fail to produce measures.
newsitem.headline: Israel budget talks fail to produce measures.

text.p: Talks on Tuesday night between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Finance Minister Dan Meridor and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel failed to yield any decisions concerning the government budget deficit.
Officials present at the meeting, who asked not to be named, said the three agreed to continue talks on the 1997 budget but they did not schedule a date for a new meeting.
It was not clear whether they would meet again before the week-long Jewish holiday of Passover which starts on April 21. The sources said it was unlikely any decisions would be reached before then.
Netanyahu, Meridor and Frenkel have met three evenings in a row in an attempt to achieve a consensus on the budget deficit.
The central bank has called for spending cuts to guarantee the government will meet its deficit target this year of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.

Treasury officials want to tie such a cut to an agreement that the central bank will lower interest rates to boost the slowing economy. Netanyahu's chief economic adviser Moshe Leon has also said any budget cut must be tied to expansionary monetary policy.
Frenkel has been reluctant to agree to such a deal and chances for a reduction in interest rates this month grew even more remote on Tuesday with the release of March inflation data, analysts said.
The Central Bureau of Statistics announced that the consumer price index in March grew by a higher-than expected 1.0 percent, following a sharp rise of 1.2 percent in February.
The 1997 budget of 197 billion shekels already includes a seven billion shekel cut. Treasury officials believe another one billion shekel cut may be needed to meet the deficit target.
Leon said that in the first quarter of the year there was a 500 million shekel deviation from the deficit target.
